guidelines.title: visible label
guidelines.rule: Place a clear label outside the field so users always know what information belongs there.

citation.source: NN/g — Placeholders in Form Fields Are Harmful; Material 3 — Text fields

pass_when: Each input has a clear label outside the field, visible before and during use.
fail_when: No outside label; the field is named only by inside text or not at all.

guidelines.title: label stays visible
guidelines.rule: Keep the label visible while the user types and checks the value; do not rely on text that disappears inside the field.

citation.source: NN/g — Placeholders in Form Fields Are Harmful; Material 3 — Text fields

pass_when: While the field has focus or a value, the label remains on screen.
fail_when: After typing starts, only the value remains; the naming text has disappeared.

guidelines.title: error identifies and fixes
guidelines.rule: Error messages identify the problem and give constructive advice so the user can fix it.

citation.source: NN/g — 10 Design Guidelines for Reporting Errors in Forms; NN/g — Website Forms Usability; Vercel Web Interface Guidelines

pass_when: On error, visible text says what is wrong and how to fix it (or the next step).
fail_when: Copy is generic, does not identify the problem, or gives no constructive advice. (Preserve-input is cited; this row checks the message, not whether the value was wiped.)

guidelines.title: placeholder hint conflict
guidelines.rule: CONFLICT — NN/g: do not use placeholder as the label; put essential hints outside the field so they stay visible. Apple HIG: a text field may show placeholder hint text to communicate purpose, and because that text disappears also include a separate label. Tidwell Input Prompt fills an empty field with a prompt of expected input; Tidwell Input Hints put an explanatory comment next to the field (NN/g side). Dual-cite; not two winners.

citation.source: NN/g — Placeholders in Form Fields Are Harmful; Apple HIG — Text fields; Apple HIG — Entering data; Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Getting Input — Input Hints; Input Prompt (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: A separate label is present. If in-field hint/prompt exists, it is extra, not the only name for the field. Essential format/help that must stay readable is also available outside the field (NN/g / Tidwell hints) without treating Apple’s extra hint as a fail.
fail_when: Placeholder or in-field prompt is the only label (agreed fail across the cites).

guidelines.title: inline after complete
guidelines.rule: Prefer inline validation after the user finishes a field; do not show an error before input is complete or on fields they have not reached.

citation.source: NN/g — 10 Design Guidelines for Reporting Errors in Forms (§1, §7)

pass_when: Field error can appear after the user finishes that field (blur/complete), without a full-form submit as the only path; no error while still typing that field; untouched later fields stay quiet.
fail_when: Errors only after full submit; or error appears mid-keystroke on the active field; or untouched fields are marked invalid.

guidelines.title: success complex fields
guidelines.rule: For complex fields, show successful entry (and instant rules as the user types) without spamming success on merely-required empty-to-filled fields.

citation.source: NN/g — 10 Design Guidelines for Reporting Errors in Forms (§2)

pass_when: A complex field (multiple rules, e.g. password) shows success and/or live rule checks; simple required fields do not get a success state for merely becoming non-empty.
fail_when: Complex field shows only errors, or every required field flashes success when filled.

guidelines.title: next to field not summary only
guidelines.rule: Put the error next to the field in error; a top validation summary must not be the only indication.

citation.source: NN/g — 10 Design Guidelines for Reporting Errors in Forms (§3, §8); Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Getting Input — Error Messages (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia); Vercel Web Interface Guidelines

pass_when: Error text sits next to the field; if a summary exists, field-level indication is also present.
fail_when: Only a distant banner, dialog, or summary list; the field itself has no error copy.

guidelines.title: not color only
guidelines.rule: Differentiate error from normal field state with color plus non-color cues (outline, weight, icon); do not rely on color alone.

citation.source: NN/g — 10 Design Guidelines for Reporting Errors in Forms (§4, §5); NN/g — Website Forms Usability

pass_when: Error state uses color and at least one non-color cue (outline, weight, icon, or error text).
fail_when: Error is only a color change (e.g. red border or red text with no other cue).

guidelines.title: modal not only copy
guidelines.rule: Use modals for form errors sparingly; do not put the only copy of a field error in a dialog that must be dismissed before the field can be fixed.

citation.source: NN/g — 10 Design Guidelines for Reporting Errors in Forms (§6)

pass_when: The field can be corrected with its error copy still available outside a must-dismiss dialog (or with no modal).
fail_when: The only field-error copy is in a modal that must be dismissed before editing the field.

guidelines.title: not tooltip only
guidelines.rule: Do not require hover or an extra click on an icon to read the error message.

citation.source: NN/g — 10 Design Guidelines for Reporting Errors in Forms (§9)

pass_when: Error message is readable without hover and without clicking an extra icon.
fail_when: Error text is only in a tooltip, title, or icon-click overlay.

guidelines.title: repeated extra help
guidelines.rule: When the same error repeats (three or more times in one attempt), provide extra help: review error patterns, refine the design, and make messages more actionable.

citation.source: NN/g — 10 Design Guidelines for Reporting Errors in Forms (§10)

pass_when: On the third-or-more same error in one attempt, the UI offers extra help and more actionable copy than the first showing.
fail_when: The same error copy repeats three or more times with no added help.

guidelines.title: replace supporting text
guidelines.rule: Swap supporting text for error text; do not stack error text on top of supporting text (layout shift).

citation.source: Material 3 — Text fields

pass_when: In error, supporting text is replaced by error text in the same slot; layout does not grow a second line under the hint.
fail_when: Error stacks on supporting text and shifts the layout.

guidelines.title: focus first error
guidelines.rule: On submit, move focus to the first field in error.

citation.source: Vercel Web Interface Guidelines — Forms

pass_when: After a failed submit, focus is on the first field in error.
fail_when: Focus stays on Submit or elsewhere, not the first error field.

guidelines.title: keep short
guidelines.rule: Keep the form short: remove fields that can be derived, collected later, or omitted.

citation.source: NN/g — Website Forms Usability

pass_when: Asked fields are needed now; derivable, deferrable, or omitable data is not on this form.
fail_when: The form asks for unused-now, already-known, or computable data.

guidelines.title: group related labels fields
guidelines.rule: Visually group related labels and fields; put each label close to its field (not equidistant from several).

citation.source: NN/g — Website Forms Usability

pass_when: Related fields share a visual group; each label is closer to its own field than to neighbors.
fail_when: Related fields are ungrouped, or a label sits equally between two controls.

guidelines.title: single column
guidelines.rule: Present fields in a single column (short related fields such as city/state/zip may share a row).

citation.source: NN/g — Website Forms Usability

pass_when: Independent fields stack in one column; only short related fields share a row.
fail_when: Unrelated fields sit in multiple columns that force a zigzag fill path.

guidelines.title: logical sequence
guidelines.rule: Sequence fields and choices in a logical, conventional order and make Tab order match that sequence.

citation.source: NN/g — Website Forms Usability

pass_when: Visual order matches a conventional task order; Tab moves in that same order.
fail_when: Fields jump topics, or Tab order disagrees with visual order.

guidelines.title: progressive disclosure
guidelines.rule: Show only what is needed at the current step; reveal further fields as the user progresses (pages or conditional logic).

citation.source: NN/g — 4 Principles to Reduce Cognitive Load in Forms

pass_when: Only the current step’s needed fields are shown; later or conditional fields appear when relevant.
fail_when: Every possible question is visible at once on a long flow with no paging or conditionals.

guidelines.title: requirements before start
guidelines.rule: Before a long form, communicate requirements up front (time, materials, deadlines, attempt limits, whether progress is saved).

citation.source: NN/g — 4 Principles to Reduce Cognitive Load in Forms

pass_when: Before the first field of a long form, time, materials, deadlines, attempt limits, and save behavior that apply are stated.
fail_when: Those requirements appear only mid-form or after failure — or not at all on a long form.

guidelines.title: progress on long forms
guidelines.rule: On long forms, show a clear progress indicator of how much is done and how much remains.

citation.source: NN/g — 4 Principles to Reduce Cognitive Load in Forms

pass_when: Long form shows done vs remaining progress.
fail_when: Long form has no progress indication.

guidelines.title: plain language
guidelines.rule: Write labels and instructions in plain language that mirrors how users talk about the information.

citation.source: NN/g — 4 Principles to Reduce Cognitive Load in Forms

pass_when: Labels/instructions use ordinary words for the asked data.
fail_when: Copy requires unexplained jargon to know what to enter.

guidelines.title: positive wording
guidelines.rule: Use positive wording; avoid negatives that force users to reverse the statement (especially opt-in checkboxes).

citation.source: NN/g — 4 Principles to Reduce Cognitive Load in Forms

pass_when: Statements (esp. opt-in checkboxes) are positive; checking means agreement with a direct statement.
fail_when: User must reverse a negative (e.g. “don’t not email me”) to opt in or out.

guidelines.title: no double barreled
guidelines.rule: Do not ask two things in one question; split double-barreled items.

citation.source: NN/g — 4 Principles to Reduce Cognitive Load in Forms

pass_when: Each question/control asks one thing.
fail_when: One item asks two things (and/or) that could disagree.

guidelines.title: distinguish optional required
guidelines.rule: Distinguish optional and required fields; limit optional fields and label them as optional.

citation.source: NN/g — Website Forms Usability

pass_when: Optional vs required is visible; optional fields are few and labeled optional.
fail_when: Mix of optional and required with no marking, or many unlabeled optionals.

guidelines.title: explain format upfront
guidelines.rule: If a field requires a specific format or type of input, state those instructions before the user fails.

citation.source: NN/g — Website Forms Usability

pass_when: Format/type instructions are visible next to the field before submit failure.
fail_when: Format is stated only in a post-submit error, or never.

guidelines.title: required before proceed
guidelines.rule: Make people understand they must provide required data before they can proceed (for example enable Next only after required fields are filled).

citation.source: Apple HIG — Entering data

pass_when: User can tell required data blocks proceed (disabled Next/Submit until required filled, or equivalent explicit gate).
fail_when: User can proceed with required fields empty and only learns on a later error, with no prior indication they must provide the data.

guidelines.title: avoid reset clear
guidelines.rule: Avoid Reset and Clear on web forms; if Cancel is needed for sensitive data, give it much less prominence than Submit.

citation.source: NN/g — Website Forms Usability

pass_when: No form-wide Reset/Clear; if Cancel exists for sensitive data, it is visually weaker than Submit.
fail_when: Reset/Clear wipes the form, or Cancel equals/competes with Submit.

guidelines.title: match control and size
guidelines.rule: Match the control and field size to the type and expected length of input (avoid dropdowns for two or three options that can be radios; size the text field to the expected value).

citation.source: NN/g — Website Forms Usability; Apple HIG — Text fields

pass_when: Two–three options are radios (not a dropdown); text field width fits typical expected length.
fail_when: Two–three options hidden in a dropdown, or a long value is clipped in a too-narrow field (or a tiny value sits in an oversized unmatched control).

guidelines.title: helpful constraints
guidelines.rule: Where acceptable values are known, constrain input so invalid data cannot be entered instead of failing later.

citation.source: NN/g — 4 Principles to Reduce Cognitive Load in Forms

pass_when: Known-valid set is constrained (picker, allowed charset, max length, stepper) so invalid values cannot be entered.
fail_when: Known-valid set is free text rejected only after entry.

guidelines.title: use device features
guidelines.rule: Populate the field from phone features when they apply (camera, GPS, voice, contacts).

citation.source: NN/g — A Checklist for Designing Mobile Input Fields

pass_when: Where camera, GPS, voice, or contacts can supply the value, that path is offered.
fail_when: Applicable device capture is typing-only.

guidelines.title: compute from other info
guidelines.rule: Compute the value from other information when you can (for example state from ZIP, skip a coupon the user does not have).

citation.source: NN/g — A Checklist for Designing Mobile Input Fields

pass_when: Values derivable from answers already given are filled or skipped (e.g. state from ZIP).
fail_when: User re-enters data the form could compute, or is forced through a field that does not apply.

guidelines.title: allow paste and drag
guidelines.rule: Allow copy/paste (never block paste) and, where the platform supports it, drag-and-drop into the field.

citation.source: NN/g — A Checklist for Designing Mobile Input Fields; Vercel Web Interface Guidelines; Apple HIG — Entering data

pass_when: Paste into the field works; copy out works; drag-and-drop works where the platform supports it.
fail_when: Paste is blocked or stripped by the field.

guidelines.title: matching keyboard and type
guidelines.rule: Show the keyboard and input type that match the content (email, tel, URL, number, and equivalent platform keyboards).

citation.source: NN/g — A Checklist for Designing Mobile Input Fields; Apple HIG — Text fields; Vercel Web Interface Guidelines

pass_when: Email/tel/URL/number (and equivalents) use matching `type`/`inputmode`/platform keyboard.
fail_when: Those contents use a generic text keyboard.

guidelines.title: no autocorrect identity fields
guidelines.rule: Do not autocorrect names, addresses, or emails; turn spellcheck off on emails, codes, and usernames.

citation.source: NN/g — A Checklist for Designing Mobile Input Fields; Vercel Web Interface Guidelines

pass_when: Name, address, email: autocorrect off. Email, code, username: spellcheck off.
fail_when: Those fields autocorrect or spellcheck as prose.

guidelines.title: allow typos abbreviations
guidelines.rule: Allow typos or abbreviations rather than rejecting near-matches the system can interpret.

citation.source: NN/g — A Checklist for Designing Mobile Input Fields

pass_when: Interpretable near-matches (typo, abbreviation) are accepted.
fail_when: Near-matches the system could interpret are rejected.

guidelines.title: forgiving format autoformat
guidelines.rule: Accept the value in whatever recognizable format the user types and autoformat it; do not force a single syntax.

citation.source: NN/g — A Checklist for Designing Mobile Input Fields; Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Getting Input — Forgiving Format (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: Recognizable variants are accepted and autoformatted.
fail_when: A single punctuation/syntax is required; other recognizable forms are rejected.

guidelines.title: structured format
guidelines.rule: When a strict syntax is required, put that structure into the control (segmented fields or visible separators) instead of a blank box.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Getting Input — Structured Format (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: Strict-syntax values use segmented fields or visible separators.
fail_when: Strict syntax is a blank box plus after-the-fact format errors only.

guidelines.title: fill in the blanks
guidelines.rule: When a label/control pair is awkward, present the request as a short sentence with blanks to fill in.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Getting Input — Fill-in-the-Blanks (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: Awkward label/control pairs are recast as a short sentence with blanks.
fail_when: The request is an awkward disconnected label+blank where a sentence-blank would fit the cited pattern.

guidelines.title: password strength meter
guidelines.rule: While a new password is typed, show a strength meter (and rules) so the user can see whether the value meets the system’s bar.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Getting Input — Password Strength Meter (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia); NN/g — 10 Design Guidelines for Reporting Errors in Forms (§2)

pass_when: During new-password entry, a meter and the rules are visible and update.
fail_when: New-password field has no meter and/or no rules while typing.

guidelines.title: autocompletion
guidelines.rule: As the user types a value with a known set of completions, suggest and complete matches.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Getting Input — Autocompletion (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia); NN/g — A Checklist for Designing Mobile Input Fields

pass_when: Known completion set: suggestions appear from typed prefix and can complete the value.
fail_when: Known set is typed from memory with no suggestions.

guidelines.title: dropdown chooser
guidelines.rule: For a bounded choice set, let the user pick from a drop-down chooser rather than typing the value from memory.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Getting Input — Drop-down Chooser (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: Bounded set is picked from a drop-down (or equivalent chooser), not typed from memory.
fail_when: Bounded list is a blank the user must recall.

guidelines.title: list builder
guidelines.rule: When the user must assemble a list of items, provide a list builder (available vs selected), not a single free-text dump.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Getting Input — List Builder (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: Assembling a list uses available-vs-selected (add/remove) UI.
fail_when: Multi-item list is one free-text dump.

guidelines.title: good defaults smart prefills
guidelines.rule: Prefill with good defaults and smart values the user can accept or edit.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Getting Input — Good Defaults and Smart Prefills (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia); NN/g — A Checklist for Designing Mobile Input Fields

pass_when: Known defaults, history, or frequent values are prefilled and editable.
fail_when: User retypes a known default/history/frequent value with no prefill.

guidelines.title: get from system
guidelines.rule: Get information from the system whenever possible; do not ask people to type data you can gather automatically or with permission.

citation.source: Apple HIG — Entering data

pass_when: Data the system can gather (auto or with permission) is gathered, not typed.
fail_when: User types data the system already has or can request.

guidelines.title: never prepopulate password
guidelines.rule: Never prepopulate a password field; ask people to enter it or use biometric or keychain authentication.

citation.source: Apple HIG — Entering data

pass_when: Password field is empty of a visible/pre-filled password; entry is typing or biometric/keychain.
fail_when: A password value is prepopulated in the field.

guidelines.title: offer choices not only text
guidelines.rule: When possible, offer choices (picker, menu, or other selection) instead of requiring text entry.

citation.source: Apple HIG — Entering data

pass_when: Where a known choice set exists, user picks (picker/menu/selection) instead of typing.
fail_when: Known choice set is text-entry only.

guidelines.title: clear button
guidelines.rule: Display a trailing Clear control so people can erase the field without repeatedly tapping Delete.

citation.source: Apple HIG — Text fields

pass_when: Filled text field shows a trailing Clear that empties that field.
fail_when: User can only erase by repeated Delete; no trailing Clear.

guidelines.title: combo box
guidelines.rule: When text input must be paired with a list of choices, use a combo box.

citation.source: Apple HIG — Text fields

pass_when: Type-plus-list task uses a combo box (text field + choice list).
fail_when: Type-plus-list is split into disconnected text and list, or list-only when typing is required.

guidelines.title: html autocomplete and name
guidelines.rule: Give inputs `autocomplete` and a meaningful `name`.

citation.source: Vercel Web Interface Guidelines — Forms

pass_when: Inputs have `autocomplete` and a meaningful `name`.
fail_when: Missing `autocomplete` or missing/meaningless `name`.

guidelines.title: shared hit target choice
guidelines.rule: Checkbox and radio label and control share a single hit target (no dead zones).

citation.source: Vercel Web Interface Guidelines — Forms

pass_when: Click/tap on label, control, or the space between toggles the same choice.
fail_when: Dead zone between control and label; only the small control hits.

guidelines.title: visible with keyboard
guidelines.rule: Keep the field visible in both orientations when the keyboard is displayed.

citation.source: NN/g — A Checklist for Designing Mobile Input Fields

pass_when: Focused field stays visible with the on-screen keyboard in portrait and landscape.
fail_when: Keyboard covers the field in an orientation so the value cannot be seen.

guidelines.title: clickable
guidelines.rule: Labels are clickable (`htmlFor` or wrapping the control).

citation.source: Vercel Web Interface Guidelines — Forms

pass_when: Activating the label focuses or toggles the associated control via `htmlFor` or wrapping.
fail_when: Label click does nothing; no association.

guidelines.title: enabled until request
guidelines.rule: Keep Submit enabled until the request starts; then show a spinner on the request.

citation.source: Vercel Web Interface Guidelines — Forms

pass_when: Submit stays enabled until the request starts; then a spinner (in-flight) shows.
fail_when: Submit is disabled before the request starts, or in-flight has no spinner.

guidelines.title: warn unsaved
guidelines.rule: Warn before navigation that would lose unsaved changes.

citation.source: Vercel Web Interface Guidelines — Forms

pass_when: Leaving with unsaved changes prompts a warning.
fail_when: Navigation discards unsaved values with no warning.
